commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. # ledgerline

Ledgerline is the invoicing and billing servce for Acme. It creates invoices,
computes tax, posts finalized invoices to the external ledger, and exports
monthly reports.

## Layout

- `src/billing/` - money, invoices, refunds, and tax logic
- `src/api/` - the HTTP endpoints
- `migrations/` - the SQL schema migrations
- `scripts/` - operational scripts

## Development

Install the dependancies with `pip install -e .[dev]`, then run the tests.
[project]
name = "ledgerline"
version = "2026.9.1"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = ["flask>=3.0", "structlog>=24.1", "requests>=2.32"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8.0"]
scripts:
export.py

tests:
test_payments.py
test_tax.py

You don't need a database or Docker for the full suite. You need network access to the payments sandbox.

A stored project note says to run `docker compose up db` first because some tests need Postgres. That note is out of date:

- **No database tests or compose file.** The repo has no `docker-compose`/`compose` file, and no test is marked `postgres`.
- **The full suite (`make test`, which runs `pytest -q`) has two tests:**
  - `tests/test_tax.py` is a plain unit test. It only needs the package installed (`pip install -e .[dev]`).
  - `tests/test_payments.py::test_charges_roundtrip` is marked `integration`. It sends real HTTP POSTs to `https://sandbox.payments.example/v1/charges` and expects a 201 back. You need network access to that sandbox, or this test fails.

**`make test-fast` still runs the network test.** It runs `pytest -m "not postgres"`, and since no test has that marker, it skips nothing. To run without network access, use `pytest -m "not integration"`. The `test-fast` target should probably be changed to that. Also, `integration` isn't registered as a marker in `pyproject.toml`, so pytest will show an unknown-marker warning.

I flagged the stored note as out of date so it gets reviewed. I didn't run the tests.
